title: Billing dispute and chargeback resolution playbook
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the operational process, SLAs, communications templates, and ownership for resolving enterprise billing disputes and chargeback requests during onboarding and the first 90 days post-go-live. It is intended for CSMs, BillingOps, Finance, Support Engineering, and Legal.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) for billing disputes, ensure consistent customer communications, protect revenue recognition, and capture audit evidence for chargebacks or credits.
- Scope: Applies to all enterprise tenants (Dedicated and Private) with contract value >= $50k ARR during onboarding and the first 90 days after go-live. Does not replace Finance-led invoicing corrections for legacy invoices; it coordinates with Finance for those cases.

Definitions:
- Dispute: A customer-initiated claim that an invoice, usage charge, or billing calculation is incorrect.
- Chargeback: A request to reverse or offset billed amount against a future invoice or issue a formal credit.
- Priority levels:
  1) P0 — Billing outage affecting all invoices or system-side errors that systematically overcharge customers; target acknowledgement < 1 business hour; remediation plan in 4 hours.
  2) P1 — Material dispute where customer-facing usage appears incorrect (>10% deviation or > $5k discrepancy); target acknowledgement < 4 business hours; resolution in 3 business days.
  3) P2 — Minor disagreement or clarification (<10% and < $5k); target acknowledgement within 1 business day; resolution in 10 business days.

Ownership and contacts:
- First responder: Customer Success Manager (CSM) — initial intake, triage, and customer comms.
- Technical validation: Support Engineering (SE) — investigates telemetry, request logs, KV/cache behavior, and model fallback records.
- Billing operations: BillingOps — recalculates usage, verifies aggregation + quota logic, prepares credits.
- Finance: Signs off on formal credits and updates AR records.
- Legal: Engaged when contractual dispute or potential revenue recognition impact.

Escalation matrix:
1) CSM escalates to SE (channel: #billing-ops-escalations, tag @oncall-se) after initial intake if P0/P1.
2) SE triages, produces technical findings and a short timeline (within 8 hours for P1).
3) If disagreement remains after technical validation, CSM opens BillingOps ticket (billing-api) and informs Finance.
4) If resolution crosses 5 business days or exceeds $50k, escalate to Director of Customer Success + Head of Billing for approval and external comms.

Operational procedure (step-by-step):
1) Intake (CSM)
   - Capture: customer contact, invoice ID, invoice date, disputed amount, business impact, and preferred remedy (credit, refund, or adjustment).
   - Assign priority (P0/P1/P2) and open the internal incident in the Customer Success ticketing queue (prefix: BILL-). Attach customer-provided artifacts (screenshots, billing CSVs).
2) Triage (CSM, within SLA for priority)
   - Verify customer identity and contract tier. Confirm invoice numbers and timeframe.
   - If P0, immediately declare incident and notify #ops-all and on-call SRE.
3) Technical investigation (SE)
   - Confirm request routing and model selection logs: check `billing-api` request logs, `ingress-gateway` traces, and `telemetry-gatekeeper` aggregation.
   - Query usage records: run query against `usage-aggregation` table (example SQL):
     SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) as total_tokens, model_name, date
     FROM usage_aggregation
     WHERE tenant_id = 'TENANT_X' AND date BETWEEN '2026-10-01' AND '2026-10-31'
     GROUP BY tenant_id, model_name, date;
   - Verify any cache-busting events, canary rollouts, or model-fanout that could double-count tokens.
   - Produce a short findings doc (one-page) that lists root-cause candidates and evidence links.
4) BillingOps reconciliation
   - Recompute the invoice using the canonical aggregation export (CSV/JSON) and the rate-card in effect for the invoice period. Maintain a checksumed export and attach to the case.
   - If code/aggregation bug found, create a paging ticket in engineering backlog with severity and request a hotfix/retroactive adjustment.
5) Proposal and customer communication (CSM + BillingOps)
   - Draft proposed remedy (credit/refund/adjustment) and the timeline for application.
   - Use the communication templates below.
6) Finance sign-off and execution
   - Finance validates credit amount, posts credit memo or refund, updates AR, and records reason codes.
   - BillingOps updates invoice metadata and attaches evidence to the ticket.
7) Closure and retrospective
   - Confirm customer acceptance, update ticket with resolution artifacts, and schedule a 1-week postmortem for P0/P1 cases.
   - Capture follow-up actions in the customer QBR if systemic.

Evidence and artifacts to collect (minimum):
- Customer-submitted dispute form or email (archive).
- Relevant invoice PDF and raw aggregation export (CSV/JSON).
- Query IDs and trace IDs from `ingress-gateway` and `billing-api` (trace links).
- Findings doc from SE and final recalculation spreadsheet with checksum.
- Finance credit memo number or refund transaction ID.

Communication templates (examples)
1) Acknowledgement (send within SLA)
Subject: Acknowledged — Billing enquiry for invoice INV-12345
Body: Hi [Customer Name],
Thank you — we have received your billing enquiry for invoice INV-12345 (amount: $X). We have opened case BILL-6789 and assigned it priority [P1]. Our technical and billing teams will investigate and we will update you inside the SLA timelines. If you have additional artifacts, please attach them to this thread.
2) Interim status (P1/P0)
Subject: Interim update — Billing enquiry INV-12345 (case BILL-6789)
Body: Hi [Customer Name],
We are actively investigating. Current findings: [short summary]. Target resolution: [date/time]. If the issue is high-impact we will provide hourly updates.
3) Resolution and credit confirmation
Subject: Resolved — Billing enquiry INV-12345 (case BILL-6789)
Body: Hi [Customer Name],
We have completed our investigation and applied the following remedy: [credit/refund/adjustment details with reference #]. The credit will appear on your next invoice (or refund dispatched on [date]). Summary of cause: [one-paragraph root cause]. Preventative steps taken: [bullet list].

Customer-facing acceptance criteria (must be documented in ticket):
- The refunded or credited amount equals the agreed remedy.
- Finance has produced a credit memo or refund transaction ID and AR is updated.
- Customer confirms acceptance in writing.

Automation and tooling recommendations:
- Automate evidence collection: attach aggregated usage export and trace IDs at intake using the `billing-intake` Lambda hook.
- Add a billing dispute webhook to notify `#billing-ops-escalations` with structured payload: {"case_id":"BILL-XXXXX","tenant_id":"T-123","priority":"P1","invoice_id":"INV-..."} (engineering backlog item: BILLING-2381).
- Maintain a shared Google Sheet (read-only for customers) for long-running reconciliations; link in the ticket.

Reporting and KPIs:
- SLA compliance: percent of disputes acknowledged within target SLA (goal >= 98%).
- MTTR by priority: target P1 <= 3 business days (rolling 90-day median).
- Error rate: percent of invoices requiring adjustment after go-live (target <= 0.5%).
- Fiscal impact: mean credit amount and top contributing root causes.

Playbook examples and edge cases:
- Duplicate charge due to canary rollback: If SE confirms double-counting tied to canary rollback, proceed with immediate credit and create an engineering incident.
- Customer claims lost feature credits (promo/discount not applied): verify contract-level entitlements and reconcile with rate card; escalate to Finance/Legal for contract amendment if needed.
- Suspected fraud / abuse: pause account billing (billing-api flag: billing_hold = true), notify Legal and follow fraud handling SOP.

Postmortem and continuous improvement:
- For P0/P1 incidents, schedule a 1-week postmortem with CSM, SE, BillingOps, and Finance. Capture root cause, corrective action, and preventive measures.
- Feed recurring root causes into the onboarding playbook and update rate-card validations in the billing pipeline.

Appendix A — Quick triage checklist (for CSMs)
1) Confirm invoice ID, disputed amount, and date range.
2) Confirm tenant tier and active contract adjustments.
3) Attach customer artifacts and create BILL- ticket.
4) Ping #billing-ops-escalations with case link for P0/P1.
5) Confirm SE assigned and expected update time.

Appendix B — Example internal Slack alert (to #billing-ops-escalations)
Payload (one-line): BILL-6789 | TENANT_T-123 | P1 | INV-12345 | $8,900 | @priya.nambiar — investigation assigned to @oncall-se. Link: <ticket_url>

Appendix C — Minimal JSON export schema for reconciliation artifacts
- ticket_id: string
- tenant_id: string
- invoice_id: string
- period_start: YYYY-MM-DD
- period_end: YYYY-MM-DD
- raw_usage_export_url: https://...
- recalculated_amount: string (decimal)
- evidence_links: [comma-separated links]

Notes and links:
- Service names referenced: billing-api, ingestion-gateway, usage-aggregation, telemetry-gatekeeper, billing-intake lambda.
- See related playbooks: tenant-finops-cutover-governance-playbook (onboarding), enterprise-cost-anomaly-detection-and-action-playbook (health & QBR).

Owner and maintenance cadence:
- Document owner: Priya Nambiar (Customer Success).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P0/P1 incident.
